causalModel.founding: Claywater Station is a mixed village at the road's water point. An Imperial well stands on the south bench. An Argonian landing stands on the north bank across the ford. The landing is older than the station.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A perennial spring lies beside a boat channel. The road fords the water there.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Two communities share the village. Neither community can hold the other's half.
causalModel.pressures: The well is Imperial-built and failing. The people of the landing will not help repair it in stone.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: The village would become one community or two villages within a generation.

districts.notes: The Imperial half on the south bench.

why.what: The well-station district holds the station house, the stable, the lean-to and the well.
why.whyHere: The Imperial half of the village keeps the well. It also keeps the road trade.
why.whyNeighbours: The well-station faces the landing across the ford. It lies along the road.
why.playerPurpose: Travellers find a bed, food for the road, a stable for a horse and water from the well.
why.microGeography: The district sits on a narrow bench between the channel and the hillside. It is raised on stone pads.

districts.notes: The Argonian half on the north strip; no Hist (see siting).

why.what: The landing hamlet has three mud huts round an open common. It has fish racks. Boats are pulled up on the bank.
why.whyHere: The landing is older than the station. Its polers came up from the mud-hut country. They built as they do at home, on the dry point by the channel.
why.whyNeighbours: The landing faces the well-station across the ford. The landing has no Hist. The tree of its people stands at Fenmarch Village (place.imperial-fringe.fenmarch-village, 1.7 km). The people of the landing go home for the hatching.
why.playerPurpose: The ford ferry for carts and beasts is run from the landing. The landing is the north-bank side of LF83.
why.microGeography: The district lies on the dry strip on the ford's north bank. The huts stand on mud pads raised a little above the channel.

parcels.orientationWhy: The station house's long wall runs with the road. Its door turns north-east onto the path from the street.

playerPurpose.note: Lodging upstairs and the well-keeper's provisions counter at the door (LF83 counter 1).

why.what: The station house is the well-keeper's home. Beds for travellers are upstairs. The provisions counter is at the door.
why.whyHere: A road station has a house where travellers sleep and buy food. This house belongs to the well-keeper.
why.whySpot: The house stands on the widest dry ground on the south bench. It is beside the well junction and square to the road.
why.whyNeighbours: The house stands behind the well and the lean-to. The fire, the well and the door are seen together from the street.
why.playerPurpose: The house offers a bed for the night and food for the road. Its counter is the first of the two counters in LF83.
why.microGeography: The bench rises to the south. The house stands on a stone pad that levels the fall of the ground.

parcels.orientationWhy: The windlass turns across the road. The bucket is drawn from the street side.

playerPurpose.note: The well keeper draws water for travellers and charges them for it. The poler at the landing charges the same travellers again.
Part of a quest takes place in the street round the well.
The crack in the well head is the clue that a quest asks the player to find.

why.what: The Imperial well has a cracked head. It stands at the junction of the street and the station path.
why.whyHere: The well is the reason for the place. It is the road's water point.
why.whySpot: The well stands on the raised bench east of the station house. It is above the road junction and the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The station house, the handcart and the lantern post stand round the well.
why.playerPurpose: Water can be drawn from the well. It is a landmark from the south road. It is the cracked well of LF83.
why.microGeography: The well stands on a levelled step on the bench. The step is 2 metres above the water and 1.5 m above the road.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs along the road frontage. It lies south of the lean-to.

why.what: A dry-stone wall runs along the station's road frontage.
why.whyHere: Imperial yards are walled on the road side.
why.whySpot: The wall stands south of the lean-to along the road verge. It leaves the well junction open.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall encloses the yard between the station house and the road.
why.playerPurpose: The wall divides the station's yard from the road.
why.microGeography: The wall follows the verge where the road climbs to the south-east.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs along the station house's long back wall. It is square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall runs along the back of the station house's pad.
why.whyHere: The house stands on a raised stone pad. The wall retains the pad's edge where the bench falls away.
why.whySpot: The wall stands along the pad's long back edge. It is two paces out from the house wall.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall encloses the pad behind the house. The end walls meet it at the corners.
why.playerPurpose: The wall is the reason the house stands level on a sloping bench.
why.microGeography: The bench falls below this edge. The wall stands tallest here.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the pad's north-east end. It is square to the house.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall runs across the north-east end of the station house's pad.
why.whyHere: This end of the pad stands highest over the slope down to the stable. Its edge needs retaining.
why.whySpot: The wall crosses the pad's north-east end, above the stable yard.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall joins the back wall at the corner. It stops short of the yard wall on the road side.
why.playerPurpose: The wall encloses the pad on the stable side. The yard ends at a wall.
why.microGeography: The ground drops toward the stable below this end.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the pad's south-west end. It is square to the house.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall runs across the south-west end of the station house's pad.
why.whyHere: The bench dips at the house's landing end. The wall stops the pad slumping there.
why.whySpot: The wall crosses the pad's end away from the stable. It stands behind the woodpile and the hen's nest.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall joins the back wall at one corner. It joins the road-side yard wall at the other.
why.playerPurpose: The wall encloses the pad on the landing side, behind the woodpile.
why.microGeography: The bench slopes away toward the landing below this end.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the stable's south end. It is square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall runs along the south side of the stable's pad.
why.whyHere: The stable's pad is cut into the ground at this end. The wall retains the bank behind the stalls.
why.whySpot: The wall stands along the pad's south edge. It is two paces out from the stable's end.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall meets the west wall at the pad's south-west corner.
why.playerPurpose: The wall holds the bank back from the stable's south end.
why.microGeography: The ground stands higher than the pad along most of this edge.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the stable's north end. It is square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall runs along the north side of the stable's pad.
why.whyHere: The pad is cut into the rising ground at the stable's north end. The wall holds the bank back from it.
why.whySpot: The wall stands along the pad's north edge, facing the station house.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall stops short of the pad's north-west corner. The gap is where the stable path turns in to the stalls.
why.playerPurpose: The wall holds the bank back from the stable's north end.
why.microGeography: The bench rises above this edge toward the station house.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs along the open front of the stalls. It is square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall runs along the west edge of the stable's pad, in front of the stalls.
why.whyHere: The pad is cut into the ground on its west side. The wall stops the slope slumping into the yard.
why.whySpot: The wall stands along the pad's west edge, a few paces out from the stalls.
why.whyNeighbours: The wall joins the north and south walls at the pad's corners.
why.playerPurpose: The wall encloses the stable's pad on the side that faces the landing.
why.microGeography: The ground rises above this end toward the bench.

parcels.orientationWhy: The poler's hut door turns south. The door faces the path down to the ford and the landing.

playerPurpose.note: The poler's home and the crossing fee (LF83 counter 2); the ferry is run from the landing below it.
The poler takes the crossing fee at the Argonian landing, a second charge on the travellers who paid at the well.

why.what: The poler's hut is where the crossing fee is paid.
why.whyHere: The people of the landing hamlet live by the crossing. The poler lives beside it.
why.whySpot: The hut stands at the east end of the north strip, above the ford's north bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The fish racks and the landing lie between the hut and the water. The common is to the west.
why.playerPurpose: The poler runs the ford ferry for carts and beasts. The hut has the second counter of LF83.
why.microGeography: The hut stands on dry ground above the channel. Its mud pad is raised clear of the wet bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: The family hut's door turns north-east to the Blackwood Road. The road bends round the hut.

playerPurpose.note: The landing family's home, where the player hears the landing's side of the argument over the well (LF83).

why.what: The family hut is where one household of the landing lives.
why.whyHere: The families of the landing live on the dry point by the channel.
why.whySpot: The hut stands west of the road on the inside of its bend. It is the driest ground on the north bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The road runs past the hut's door. The landing and the poler's hut lie across the road to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The hut is a home that can be entered. Its household can talk about the well and the landing.
why.microGeography: The hut stands on dry ground on a mud pad raised clear of the wet bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: The store hut's door faces east onto the store path. The door is a few metres above the landing's dock where the catch comes ashore.

why.what: The net and basket maker of the landing works in the store hut. The stored catch lies beside the workshop.
why.whyHere: A landing needs its nets mended. Its baskets are woven close to the boats.
why.whySpot: The hut stands north of the landing steps on the dry bank, clear of the road.
why.whyNeighbours: The landing steps run past the hut's door. The poler's hut stands to the south-west.
why.playerPurpose: The hut is a workshop on the landing with a door that opens.
why.microGeography: The hut stands on dry bank a metre above the channel. Its pad is raised clear of the wet ground.

playerPurpose.note: The crafter's household, where the player hears how the landing lives off the catch and the crossing.

parcels.orientationWhy: The raft lies with its long side to the bank. Travellers can board from the bank.

why.what: The ferry raft is moored in the channel east of the landing.
why.whyHere: Carts and beasts cross on the raft. The hull stays afloat by the landing.
why.whySpot: The raft lies in the nearest water that floats it. The water is at least a metre deep all round, east of the road.
why.whyNeighbours: The cleats on the bank hold the raft. The landing path runs to it.
why.playerPurpose: The ferry carries carts, beasts and travellers across the ford.
why.microGeography: The channel water stands at 35.24 m. It is more than a metre deep round the hull.

parcels.orientationWhy: The open stalls face west-south-west into the walled paddock. Their backs are to the road.

why.what: The stable is open and has four stalls. Travellers' horses stand there for the night.
why.whyHere: A road station has a stable for animals that cannot come inside.
why.whySpot: The stable stands on the levelled yard south-east of the station house, walled on three sides. No other ground near the road is level and wide enough for the stalls and a paddock.
why.whyNeighbours: Stone walls enclose the paddock in front of the stalls on three sides. The station house stands to the north-west.
why.playerPurpose: A traveller's horse can be stabled here for the night.
why.microGeography: The stable stands on a levelled yard cut into the foot of the hillside.

parcels.orientationWhy: The two dock spans run from the dry bank straight out to the raft's berth.

why.what: The landing stage is two plank dock spans on piles. They run from the bank out over the channel.
why.whyHere: The ferry raft needs a dry way out to water deep enough to float it.
why.whySpot: The stage starts at the bank east of the poler's hut. It is the shortest way to a metre of water.
why.whyNeighbours: The raft lies at the stage's end. The cleats and the canoe are at its foot.
why.playerPurpose: The stage is the way from the bank to the ferry raft.
why.microGeography: The deck stands a hand's breadth above the channel. The deck's piles go down into the channel bed.

routes.why: The Blackwood Road runs between the well junction and the ford. Both halves of the village face this street.
This route runs from the street to the station house door.
This route is the short worn step from the road to the well head.
This route starts at the well junction. It runs round the outside of the north yard wall. It then enters at the yard's west side. It ends at the open front of the stalls.
This route runs from the ford's north bank past the fish racks. It ends at the moored raft.
This route runs from the landing path on the ford's north bank. It climbs to the poler's pod house.
This route runs from the poler's path across the common. It ends at the family hut's door.
This route runs from the common west along the strip. It ends at the store hut.

approaches.sequence: A traveller coming down the road from the south-east sees the station house roof and its smoke first. The well at the junction and the lean-to by the fire come next. The ford and the huts beyond come into view at the junction.
approaches.wayfinding: The road runs past the yard wall to the well junction. The station house path leaves the street at the well junction.

approaches.sequence: A traveller coming from the north-west sees the hut domes and the landing lanterns first. The road passes between the huts to the ford. The well roof shows across the water.
approaches.wayfinding: The road runs through the landing to the ford. The poler's hut stands on the bank above the ford.

networkTerminals.why: The Blackwood Road arrives from Gideon. It runs along the bench to the south-east.
The road leaves the ford's north bank toward Blackwood. It passes through the landing.

combatSpaces.why: The street between the well and the ford is the combat space. A road fight at the station happens there.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The place follows the type recipe road-station-village, which has a keeper and travellers. The record's occupants are D1 family, few. The record's occupants also include D2 travellers, few. The roster file npcs.json lists a well-keeper and a poler.
scaleGrounding.why: Two named keepers and one landing family live at Claywater Station. Travellers come and go. Six buildings stand, three in the well-station and three in the landing. The dry ground holds no seventh building. The well, the lean-to and the ferry raft stand beside the buildings. Dry-stone walls hold the two station pads.

candidates.why: This candidate is the only dry ground on both banks of the ford. The south bench holds the well-station. The north strip holds the landing.
This candidate is the flat pad east of the road beside the channel.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The east side has one flat pad east of the road. The rest of the east side is open water at 35.24 m. The east side has no room for either half of the village.

exceptions.reason: No third linked Argonian shell with a usable cell exists. The mudhut02 shell (KeebaHouseElder) was tried in the residual round. Its door stands 4.7 m above the ground at every scanned pose. The kit has no stair or walkway to reach that door. The store keeps its King of the Murkmire pod.
